data.long_meaning: In Islamic history, Abbasah is known as the mother of the Prophet Muhammad's (PBUH) cousin and companion, Ali ibn Abi Talib (RA). She was a devoted and supportive wife and a loving mother to her children and the Muslim community. The name Abbaasah carries the meaning “Mother of the believers” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Abbaasah usually hope their child will grow to embody mother of the believers and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.cultural_impact: Abbasah is a significant name in Islamic history, especially because of her unwavering support for the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) and his cousin and successor, Ali ibn Abi Talib (RA). She was a devoted wife to her husband, Abdul Muttalib, and a loving mother to her children, including Ali. Her story serves as an example of a strong, faithful, and nurturing woman in Islamic tradition.
data.spiritual_significance: In the Islamic context, Abbasah's name holds deep spiritual significance as a symbol of maternal love, devotion to family, and unwavering support for the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) and his community. Her name also serves as a reminder of the importance of solid familial and community bonds in Islamic teachings and values. Additionally, her story illustrates the belief in the spiritual significance of mothers and the profound impact they can have on shaping the lives of their children and future generations.

historical_references.context: Abbas ibn Abd al-Muttalib is the uncle of Prophet Muhammad and the father of Imam Ali Zain al-Abidin. He played a significant role in the early Islamic history by taking care of Prophet Muhammad during his childhood and supporting him throughout his life. He was also one of the ten companions who were given the title 'As-Sahabah Ar-Rashidun' (The Rightly Guided Caliphs).

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Al-Bukhari and Muslim, Sahih, Book 38, Hadith 46. The name Abbaasah carried significant weight in that era.
historical_references.context: Abbas ibn Ali, the grandson of Abbas ibn Abd al-Muttalib, was martyred during the Battle of Karbala in 680 CE while fighting for his brother Imam Hussein against the Umayyad army led by Yazid ibn Mu'awiyah. His courage and loyalty to his brother earned him great respect and admiration in Islamic history.
